transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I start out really motivated, but I keep zoning out when people explain what to do and end up not finishing my class assignments or business tasks the way they were asked. It's just making it really hard to keep up with my college classes and my online shop.
Do you find it hard to focus or pay attention to details even when you're doing things that you enjoy or find interesting?

Yes, definitely. Even with my online accessories shop, which I absolutely love, I'll start a new product listing or make inventory with so much excitement. But midway through, I'll space out or get pulled into a different idea, leaving the work half-finished.
Do you often feel sad, empty, or depressed, or have you experienced a loss of interest in activities that you once enjoyed?

No, I don't really feel sad or depressed, and I definitely haven't lost interest in my shop—I still really want to do it! My struggle is much more about staying focused, keeping organized, and managing my constant restlessness rather than feeling down.
Do you often act on impulse, blurting out answers or interrupting others, or do impulsive behaviors, like spending money or making decisions without thinking them through, get you into trouble?

Yes, I constantly blurt out answers and finish people's sentences in class and conversations because I get impatient and feel like I already know where they're going. I also make impulsive decisions with my business, like overcommitting to collaborations and buying inventory that I don't finish, which has caused me to lose quite a bit of money.
Can you describe how you behave in quiet or low-stimulation environments, such as a library or a quiet room, and do you find yourself often fidgeting or feeling restless in these settings?

Quiet places are really hard because I feel this constant, restless pressure in my body, like I have to be moving. I'm always fidgeting—tapping my fingers or jiggling my leg—and trying to sit still feels physically uncomfortable, like energy crawling under my skin. I often have to get up and pretend to get water or use the restroom because staying planted in one spot is just too difficult.
Do you experience this restlessness and fidgeting at night as well, making it hard for you to fall asleep or stay asleep?
I'm not really sure about that, as I haven't paid much attention to how it affects my sleep. I haven't really noticed or thought about whether the restlessness keeps me awake at night.

Can you tell me more about how these symptoms affect your daily life, particularly in terms of relationships, work, or other activities, and have you noticed any significant differences in your behavior or ability to function in different settings or situations?

These issues have caused me to fail accounting, drop classes, and lose money on late shipments and half-finished inventory, while also straining conversations because I impatiently blurt out answers and finish people's sentences. It's a huge shift from high school art and shop classes where my fast-paced, hands-on style was actually praised and accommodated. Now, the structured college environment and stepwise business tasks completely clash with how my brain works.
Can you tell me more about your physical activity level as a child, such as whether you were always on the go, had trouble sitting still, or were more active than your peers?

Yes, I was definitely always on the go and had a hard time sitting still as a kid. Back in elementary school, my teachers would constantly comment about me getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, and rushing through projects. My parents even used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped moving.

Did you exhibit more symptoms of hyperactivity, such as running, climbing, or feeling constantly 'on the go,' or more symptoms of inattention, like disorganization and lack of persistence, as a child?

I had a mix of both, but the hyperactivity was definitely very prominent. My parents used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped moving, and my teachers always noted how I constantly got out of my seat and talked over others. At the same time, I also showed inattention by rushing through school projects and leaving them unfinished.

As you look back, did you find that your difficulties with staying on task and completing projects, or your hyperactive behaviors like fidgeting and restlessness, caused you more problems in your daily life and relationships?

The difficulties with staying on task and completing projects have definitely caused the most significant problems in my life. While I'm still very fidgety, those physical behaviors were actually tolerated or even helpful in my hands-on high school classes. But zoning out and leaving things half-finished has led to major consequences now, like failing accounting, dropping classes, and losing money on my shop.

Can you estimate how often your symptoms of inattention, such as zoning out or not finishing tasks, and hyperactivity, like fidgeting or impulsive decisions, occur, and how much they interfere with your daily functioning and relationships?

These symptoms happen constantly on a daily basis whenever I try to sit still for a lecture or work on my business, and it's been a major struggle for a little over two years now since starting college. It has severely impacted my life, causing me to fail my accounting class, drop other courses, and lose money on half-finished inventory, which has completely stalled my business.

You've mentioned both difficulties with staying on task and physical restlessness, but can you tell me which of these symptoms has been more persistent and problematic for you throughout your life, from childhood to the present?

Both have been with me since childhood, back when my parents called me a "wind-up toy" and teachers complained about me getting out of my seat and rushing through projects. While the physical restlessness was tolerated or even helpful in high school art classes, the difficulty staying on task and zoning out has definitely become the most problematic and disruptive issue over the last two years since starting college and my business.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus during tasks or play activities, before the age of 12?

Yes, I definitely had those issues before age 12. Back in elementary school, my teachers would always comment on me rushing through projects without finishing them, along with constantly getting out of my seat and talking over other kids. My parents even used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped moving.
Can you describe how your hyperactive symptoms, such as fidgeting or feeling restless, have changed or persisted from childhood to adulthood?

When I was a kid, my hyperactivity was very outward—I was always getting out of my seat and my parents called me a "wind-up toy." As an adult, it has shifted to a constant internal restlessness that I try to manage by fidgeting, like jiggling my leg, tapping my fingers, or twisting my hair. I still really struggle to stay seated, though, and frequently pop up during lectures just to move around.

Can you compare how your symptoms of inattention, such as zoning out or not finishing tasks, and your hyperactive symptoms, like fidgeting or restlessness, have impacted your daily life and relationships over time, and which one has been more consistently problematic for you?

My hyperactive symptoms like restlessness and fidgeting have been around since childhood, but they were mostly tolerated or seen as positive energy in high school art classes. However, my inattention symptoms, like zoning out and leaving tasks half-finished, have become much more consistently damaging over the last two years. Since starting college and trying to run my business, those focus issues have directly caused me to fail classes and lose money, making them far more problematic now.

Can you confirm whether your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus, and hyperactivity, like fidgeting or restlessness, have been present and caused significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning consistently since childhood, or did they significantly impact your life more noticeably after entering college?

The hyperactive behaviors were definitely present in childhood, back when my teachers complained about me getting out of my seat and my parents called me a wind-up toy. However, they only became a major, noticeable impairment about two years ago when I started college and tried to run my online shop. High school was much more accommodating of my active style, so the real struggles didn't hit until recently.

Can you clarify if your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity have been consistently present and problematic since childhood, or did they emerge or significantly worsen around the time you started college?

They have definitely been present since childhood, back when my teachers complained about me getting out of my seat and rushing through projects, and my parents called me a "wind-up toy." However, they became much more problematic and noticeable about two years ago when I started college business courses and tried to run my online shop. The highly structured environment and complex tasks really clashed with my habits, making it impossible to keep up.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been present since childhood but became more problematic in college. Can you confirm if you experienced significant symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity before the age of 7?

Yes, they definitely go back to early elementary school, around age six or so. Back then, my teachers would write comments about me constantly getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, and rushing through projects without finishing them. My parents also used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped moving.

Can you specify if there was a particular period or age when your symptoms of inattention, such as zoning out, and hyperactivity, like restlessness, first became noticeable to you or others, and how they have evolved over time?

They first became noticeable in early elementary school, when my teachers complained about me getting out of my seat and my parents joked I was like a wind-up toy. My active, fast-paced style was actually praised in high school art and shop classes, but the problems became a major issue about two years ago. That's when I started structured community college business courses and tried to run my online shop, which required a lot more sustained focus and organization.

Can you confirm if your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity have been consistently present and caused significant impairment since childhood, and if they have persisted into adulthood without any significant remission?

Yes, they have been present since childhood, when my teachers complained about me getting out of my seat and rushing projects, and my parents compared me to a wind-up toy. They have persisted straight into adulthood without any break, becoming a major, continuous obstacle over the last two years since I started my college business courses and online shop.

Can you confirm if your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity have been consistently present and caused significant impairment since childhood, and if they have persisted into adulthood without any significant remission or change in severity?

Yes, they've been present since elementary school, back when teachers noted I couldn't stay in my seat and my parents compared me to a wind-up toy. While my active style was tolerated in high school art classes, the symptoms became a major struggle and caused real impairment about two years ago when I started college business courses and tried to run my shop. They have been constant and challenging ever since.

Can you confirm if your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity have been consistently present and caused significant impairment since childhood, and if they have persisted into adulthood without any significant remission, considering that F90.0 typically has an onset before 7 years old and F90.1 has an onset after 7 years old?

Yes, they definitely started in early childhood, well before age seven. Back in elementary school, my teachers always complained about me getting out of my seat, talking over others, and rushing through work, and my parents joked I was like a "wind-up toy." Although it was tolerated in high school because of my hands-on art classes, these issues have persisted and became a major obstacle over the last two years since I started college and tried to run my business.
